//: One source of truth for the per-plugin CI lanes. Read by integrations/tooling/lanes.mjs, which .github/workflows/ci.yml and integrations/tooling/run-lane.mjs both go through. See integrations/PARALLEL_LANES.md.
sharedIndexNote: Port block for the CI jobs that are not a plugin lane — the hosting-surface check and the generic plugin-system e2e suite. A reserved index rather than a separate fixed block, so there is one port formula and lanes.test.mjs can prove it collides with nothing. No lane may take index 9.

lanes.note: Executable OCM discovery, bounded metadata parser and reviewed Atomic document receipt importer. Network receipt remains unavailable pending host authorization and writes; no live interoperability claim.

e2e drives the Calendar drive app (integrations/calendar/app/) in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar, choose a calendar, import and refresh through the host proxy relay, then preview and send edits with If-Match (atomic-server#1657's ifMatch, in the pin), against the mock proxy's stateful google-calendar fixture and its test drivers.

paths: devonian/github-issues/ imports the devonian package from source (vitest.config.ts aliases it to devonian/src/main.ts), so a devonian change runs this lane too. Its tests ran in devonian CI before the lens moved here. The e2e drives the GitHub issues drive app (app/, npm devonian from app/package.json) through the host's proxy relay (atomic-server#1657, in the pin) against the mock proxy's seeded atomic-fixture/tracker repository.
QuickJS partial Solid resource bridge: reviewed Atomic document import, public reads, RDF validation and fail-closed host gaps.
Executable QuickJS handle-to-DID route checks and reproducible bundle; no live resolver verification.

e2e drives the Bank statements importer through the host's generic file entry point (atomic-server#1653: manifest accepts/destination, PluginPage Import tab): publish, discover, set up, MT940 and camt.053 import, reload, reimport, local edit, conflict and refused files. The pin includes that change (atomic-server#1691); against an older host, publishing the bundle fails on the unknown manifest field. No typecheck/unit tier: money has an atomicCertification block, so the unsharded certification step in shared-checks already runs exactly its typecheck (tsconfig.json) and unit (vitest.config.ts) on every integrations/** change, plus bundle reproducibility. moneybird is listed for a future Moneybird fixture in integrations/money/fixtures/moneybird/ (plugin-specific files stay in the plugin folder); integrations/money/ has no Moneybird runtime code.

The e2e drives the Notion drive plugin (integrations/notion/app/) through the host's integration-proxy relay (store.proxy, consent bar and connect return) from ontola/atomic-server#1657, against the shared mock proxy's notion fixture. The live tier stubs fetch in-process.
Willow25 unsigned Entry codecs and Atomic signing-candidate export, verified against official encoding vectors. No Meadowcap signing, transport, WGPS or live interoperability.

e2e drives the Pets drive app (integrations/pets/app/) in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar and the mock proxy, then import through the host proxy relay (#52). It needs an .atomic-server-ref that includes the relay (atomic-server#1657, for #1624, merged into feat/plugin-debug; the pin has it); against an older pin the app reports that the host cannot reach the proxy and the spec fails at 'Not connected'.
Executable RDF interchange and reviewed Atomic snapshot storage; no live NextGraph broker verification.

The e2e drives the timesheets drive app (integrations/timesheets/app/) in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar and the mock proxy, set up workspace and look-back in the frame, then import, reload, refresh and recover from a proxy failure through the host relay (atomic-server#1657; the pin has it). Provider changes and failures go through the mock proxy's local-only fixture driver (POST /__fixture/clockify). The install is test-side (New app + replaced source) until #94. The old upstream Clockify tests were deleted in atomic-server 4bab16ee6 with the UI they drove (#44).

Willow drop importer (#139), a sandbox job like money: no provider, so no mock proxy (platforms is empty). typecheck and unit are lane tiers rather than certify.mjs's, because certification requires named atomic-server sandbox tests that do not exist for this package; the unit tier also checks that the committed plugin.js is a fresh esbuild bundle. The e2e publishes the bundle and imports fixture drops through the host's generic file entry point (atomic-server#1653, in the pin), so the QuickJS sandbox runs the Ed25519 and WILLIAM3 code and a binary file crosses the text-only hand-over. The fixtures come from willow25 (fixtures/generate/), which CI does not run.

A tooling lane (#134), not a plugin: it lives in integrations/tooling/ (`dir`) and runs only when one of its `paths` changes, not on every tooling or shared change, because each run builds atomic-server with the feature (or pulls its image). Its node tests run in shared-checks like every tooling test. It tests the gates of docs/design/server-plugin-routes.md section 0 against atomic-server built with the `plugin-routes` feature (atomic-server#1726, #1732). pluginRoutes runs the e2e twice, first at `--plugin-routes read-only`, then at `off`, on a fresh server over the same store. The spec publishes the gated fixture plugin (integrations/tooling/fixtures/gated-plugin/) and checks the `requires` and `hostFeatures` /plugin-catalog reports. At read-only it pins it, installs it through the store's review dialog and requests its drive-prefix route, which answers the fixture's body. At off, pinning is refused with host-feature-unavailable, the review dialog's Install button is disabled, and the installation from the read-only run, now degraded, answers 404. Needs an .atomic-server-ref with atomic-server#1726, #1732, #1749 and #1751.

A tooling lane (#177), not a plugin: it runs only when the shared ontology (ontology/, ontology-kit/), the dev-server that serves it, or the pin changes. Its node tests (ontology-kit/*.test.mjs) run in shared-checks. The e2e checks that the pinned host reads a generated class (event-v1) from the dev-server's /ontology/ path, which serves the committed term files with their subjects moved to its own origin and GitHub Pages' headers, and that atomic-server accepts a hand-made table of that class and a row with one of its properties. With ATOMIC_SERVER_IMAGE set the spec uses host.docker.internal, so the server in Docker fetches the same URL as the browser.
